scope: Token risk screening, transaction safety and custody/signing controls
method: Official pages/docs reviewed where available. Marketing claims are not independently validated; no wallets, credentials or signing services were connected.

discoveries: Security product offers transaction and wallet threat detection/simulation for web3 applications.
Coverage is chain/product specific and needs API/version review.
patterns: Run transaction risk simulation before user approval where available.
Preserve simulation input, result, time and policy version.
overlap: Advisory security layer only; does not replace SYLPH risk authorization.
risks: Simulation can miss state changes and novel threats.
Provider outage must fail closed or defer, not silently approve.
validation: Check exact Solana support and supported transaction versions.
Test malicious and benign transaction fixtures plus timeout behavior.

provenance: Official Blowfish product site entry; exact current developer API not fully validated.
discoveries: Transaction simulation and wallet security are marketed for detecting harmful signing actions.
Simulation provides an estimate of effects, not a guarantee of future execution state.
patterns: Decode and display expected account/token effects before signing.
Compare simulation to the exact bytes and blockhash later submitted.
overlap: Potential advisory security check without custody authority.
risks: Simulation state may be stale or differ from landed execution.
Unsupported instructions/programs can reduce detection.
validation: Verify supported Solana transaction formats and API contract.
Test malformed, unknown-program and changed-state cases.

discoveries: Range describes security, access controls, encryption and scoped integrations for financial workflows.
Public page does not establish specific token-level Solana detection coverage.
patterns: Use least-privilege read-only/scoped access for portfolio and risk data.
Maintain explicit integration permissions and audit trails.
overlap: Possible governance/security reference; no runtime execution role established.
risks: Product claims and coverage require independent assurance review.
External wallet connectivity increases data exposure.
validation: Review security reports, contracts and access controls before connecting accounts.
Use synthetic/read-only scope for evaluation.

provenance: Official Hypernative product site entry; exact Solana feature/API coverage not established here.
discoveries: Product category is real-time risk/threat monitoring for blockchain operations.
Alerting and monitoring outputs require their own confidence/freshness treatment.
patterns: Use independent alerts as secondary incident signals.
Record signal provenance and correlate with on-chain state.
overlap: Monitoring layer only; no trade authorization authority.
risks: False positives/negatives and chain coverage limitations.
Automated response can create unsafe side effects.
validation: Verify Solana coverage and alert delivery semantics.
Test with replayed incidents; keep alert response human/policy-controlled.

provenance: Official TxShield site entry; API support and product claims not independently verified.
discoveries: Listed as transaction security/preflight resource.
Exact supported chains, simulation method and data retention require documentation.
patterns: Require byte-level transaction inspection and expected account-delta checks.
Treat provider decision as an additional signal, never sole authorization.
risks: Unverified API semantics and support.
Fail-open behavior could undermine controls.
validation: Confirm official docs, supported formats and service terms.
Test timeout, unknown instruction and altered transaction cases.

provenance: Official CertiK Skynet site entry; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Security dashboard aggregates project/token risk and audit information.
A project score or audit badge cannot prove token liquidity, transferability or current safety.
patterns: Treat third-party scores as source-linked advisory metadata.
Verify contract/program and mint identity before associating an audit.
overlap: Research signal only; no market/authority overlap.
risks: Audit scope may not cover deployed program or current upgrade state.
Scores can be stale and incomplete.
validation: Inspect audit scope/date and verify program/mint addresses.
Cross-check with on-chain authorities, liquidity and holders.

provenance: Official Spearbit site entry; specific audit reports require project-level inspection.
discoveries: Security firm/network provides smart-contract security review services.
Audit conclusions are bounded by code revision, scope, assumptions and remediation status.
patterns: Bind audit references to exact source commit and deployed program binary.
Track unresolved findings and upgrade authority separately.
overlap: External audit evidence can inform code review but does not certify SYLPH runtime.
risks: Audit scope mismatch and post-audit code changes.
No audit prevents all vulnerabilities.
validation: Review report, code hash, deployment address and remediation evidence.
Run deterministic tests and independent source review.

provenance: Official Sec3 product site entry; detailed tool/version scope not verified in this pass.
discoveries: Solana ecosystem security company/product category includes program auditing and automated analysis.
Exact supported analyzers and current service offerings need version-level confirmation.
patterns: Combine static checks, fuzzing and manual program review for on-chain components.
Pin audit artifacts to commit/program deployment.
overlap: Security assurance reference; no direct application runtime role.
risks: Scanner coverage and audit scope can be misunderstood.
Third-party service terms and data sharing need review.
validation: Verify current product documentation and report scope.
Reproduce relevant findings with local tests.

discoveries: Wallet infrastructure offers policy engine, scoped sessions and transaction signing features.
Product supports external Solana wallet connectivity as well as embedded wallet workflows.
patterns: Use short-lived scoped sessions and explicit policy boundaries.
Keep signing policy independently reviewed and auditable.
overlap: Hosted signing would materially change custody architecture and is not a routine integration.
risks: External signer changes threat model, availability and key control.
Policy misconfiguration can authorize excessive actions.
validation: Do not connect capital without separate architecture/security approval.
Prototype with test keys and prove policy denial, session expiry and audit evidence.

provenance: Official Privy Solana wallet announcement and product page; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Embedded wallet infrastructure supports Solana and server-side/delegated signing features.
Wallet provisioning and delegated signing introduce an external custody/control boundary.
patterns: Use explicitly scoped authorization and read-only workflows where possible.
Separate user-wallet UX from trading-engine signer policy.
overlap: No direct engine integration justified; current signing controls remain in place.
risks: Delegated signing can expand blast radius.
Provider policy, account recovery and availability need due diligence.
validation: Review current Solana docs, SOC/security evidence and permissions.
Test only ephemeral non-capital keys with explicit denial cases.

provenance: Official Fordefi product site entry; detailed Solana API/custody scope not reviewed.
discoveries: Institutional digital-asset wallet/custody and policy control product category.
API signing and transaction policy features require current contract and supported-chain review.
patterns: Treat institutional signer as a separate authority boundary with dual control and limits.
Require complete signed intent and audit trail.
overlap: Possible custodian integration only after explicit architecture decision.
risks: Would alter signing custody and availability model.
Policy or API errors could create high-impact unauthorized actions.
validation: Do not connect live capital during research.
Review contracts, permissions, recovery, limits and test environment before any proposal.

provenance: Official Fireblocks custody principles/product pages; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Fireblocks describes institutional digital-asset custody and transaction policy workflows.
Its published model emphasizes customer key control and configurable policies; product claims require independent assurance review.
patterns: Keep transaction policy tied to destination, asset, amount and source.
Use dual control and immutable approval/audit records for treasury operations.
overlap: Institutional custody option, not a drop-in runtime dependency.
risks: Custody integration changes architecture, permissions and operational dependencies.
Policy setup and signer availability are critical.
validation: Review current Solana support, contract, security reports and recovery flows.
Test-only environment must prove policy denials and signer isolation.

provenance: Official AWS KMS product and Sign API docs; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: KMS supports asymmetric signing for selected key types/algorithms and IAM/key-policy authorization.
API requires recording key identity and signing algorithm for verification.
patterns: Use least-privilege key policies and audit signing calls.
Verify that Solana's required Ed25519 message-signing flow is supported before selecting KMS.
overlap: May support release/artifact signing; Solana transaction signer compatibility must be separately proven.
risks: Not all key algorithms/key services are compatible with Solana Ed25519 signing.
Remote signing adds latency, IAM and availability dependencies.
validation: Check supported key specs/algorithms and exact raw-message semantics.
Test public-key/address derivation and signatures against Solana libraries using non-capital test keys.

discoveries: Wallet documentation describes transaction simulation warnings and token signals including liquidity and holder concentration.
Wallet warnings are protective indicators, not complete safety verification.
patterns: Inspect transaction preview and independently verify token mint/pool.
Use separate hot wallet for risky activity and protect recovery credentials.
overlap: Wallet UX/security reference; not part of SYLPH signing pipeline.
risks: User can override warnings and simulation may be incomplete.
Phishing and malicious approvals remain possible.
validation: Use only official domains/apps and verify transaction on-chain.
Keep wallet and long-term assets separated.

discoveries: Wallet describes transaction guards, scam-site protections and hardware wallet support.
The provider explicitly notes automated checks cannot catch every threat.
patterns: Use hardware-backed custody for long-term assets and a limited hot wallet for risky interactions.
Treat wallet simulation as a layer, not a guarantee.
overlap: Wallet security reference; no engine integration.
risks: Wallet protection is endpoint/user dependent.
Seed phrase theft or malicious approvals can bypass product checks.
validation: Verify domain and hardware signing path.
Review exact transaction and confirm resulting signature/account deltas.
